title: Swiss NCSC confirms cyberattacks by AI agents on companies and critical infrastructure operators
date_note: The NCSC page gives only its publication day, 24 November 2026; it does not date the attacks.
geo_basis: agency, Switzerland; the page names no victim city
summary: The Swiss NCSC says it has for the first time confirmed cyberattacks in Switzerland carried out with AI agents against companies and critical infrastructure operators. It says the agents exploited weak or easily guessed passwords and known vulnerabilities in internet-connected systems, and that in every known case they compromised the victim's IT systems. It says the victims span at least two sectors and does not name them.
plain: Switzerland's cyber agency says AI agents were used to attack Swiss companies and critical infrastructure operators, and in every case it knows of, the victim's IT systems were compromised.
exec: The NCSC says AI-agent attacks hit Swiss companies and critical infrastructure operators, exploiting weak passwords and known flaws in internet-connected systems.
action: The NCSC advises limiting internet-facing systems, protecting internet-accessible resources such as webmail and VPN with multi-factor authentication or passkeys, and installing critical updates for internet-facing systems quickly.
impact: Confirmed compromises of IT systems at organisations in at least two sectors; sectors and victims not named.

sources.name: Swiss NCSC (BACS): Cyberattacks involving AI agents

key_findings: First time the NCSC has confirmed cyberattacks in Switzerland carried out with AI agents against companies and critical infrastructure operators.
Attackers used agentic offensive frameworks that exploit weak or easily guessed passwords and known vulnerabilities in internet-connected systems.
In every known case the AI agents led to a successful compromise of the victim's IT systems.
Victims span at least two sectors; the page does not name them.
recommendations: Limit internet-facing systems and restrict access.
Install critical updates for internet-facing systems quickly.
Protect internet-accessible internal resources with MFA or passkeys.
Grant lowest possible privileges and monitor for behavioural deviations.

validation.note: Primary source: the Swiss NCSC's own page.
